SMTO-EXE-0047 — SMTO can't safely release the earlier job right now

GUID: 36e8306f-b25e-4136-a033-f76667d52a8d
Slug: resource-reset-not-eligible
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: exe

What happened

  • You asked SMTO to forcefully release an earlier job, but that job is in a state where releasing it isn't safe. SMTO kept the earlier job's hold in place, so the waiting command hasn't run.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait a moment, then read the status line on the task's recovery card, which says whether the earlier job is running, ended or unknown. The earlier job's state may have changed since you chose to release it, and the card shows the current state.
  2. If Wait until the job state changes is available, select it. SMTO will continue on its own when the earlier job lets go. Waiting is the safe path when SMTO can't yet release the earlier job.
  3. If you started this from Settings › Operate › Reset, select Refresh owners and use only the actions shown for that row. The list there is rebuilt from the current state, so it only offers actions that are allowed now.
  4. Before asking SMTO to repeat any change, check the file, service or machine the earlier job was working on to see whether the change already happened. Don't stop programs there yourself. SMTO can't confirm what the earlier job did, and ending the wrong program could cause damage or apply a change twice.

What success looks like

  • The card shows that the earlier job has ended or its hold was released, and the task continues.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO and the Gateway computer. Don't delete SMTO files or try to release the job again until the card or the Reset page offers the option.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway refused the reset (resource_reset_not_eligible) because at least one recorded blocker is neither reset-eligible nor covered by an existing applicable reset decision.

What this means

  • Reset validation found that one or more current blockers were neither eligible for reset nor already covered by an applicable reset decision. Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.

Why this can happen

  • Reset validation found that one or more current blockers were neither eligible for reset nor already covered by an applicable reset decision.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect each blocker's current revision, liveness, claim and reset eligibility; do not erase evidence to make the action available.

How to fix it

  • Refresh the blocker state (the run's resource-reconciliation refresh, or Refresh owners in Settings › Operate › Reset) and act only on the actions offered for the current blocker revision. Do not kill processes by PID outside SMTO, delete job receipts or edit Gateway job state to force reset eligibility.
  • Refresh the blocker status and use only actions offered for its current revision. Do not terminate an uncorrelated process or erase a receipt to force eligibility.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • Only a currently eligible supported recovery action proceeds against matching recorded owners.

What not to do

  • Do not infer successful termination from a missing response, target another PID, or replay the blocked operation.

Technical notes

  • Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
